blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: A Go module records an import path and dependency requirements in `go.mod`. Create one with `go mod init`, format source with `gofmt`, run packages with `go run`, build with `go build`, and test with `go test`. Every source file begins with a package declaration; executable programs use package `main` and a `main` function. Imported names start with the package qualifier. Go rejects unused imports and local variables, keeping builds explicit. Read the earliest relevant diagnostic, correct one cause, format, and rebuild rather than running stale output.

Test the contract with build and runtime evidence

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Go is statically typed and gives every variable a zero value. Short declaration `:=` is for function bodies and must introduce at least one new name. Numeric conversions are explicit and may still lose range or precision, so validate before converting. `strconv.Atoi` and related functions return a value and an error. Handle the error before using the value; do not discard it merely to shorten code. Wrap errors with `%w` when adding context so callers can inspect the original cause. Reserve panics for unrecoverable programmer or initialization failures, not normal invalid input.

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Go uses `if`, `switch`, and one looping construct, `for`. Conditions do not use parentheses and must be boolean. `&&` and `||` short-circuit. An `if` can include a short initialization whose names remain scoped to its branches. Switch cases break automatically unless explicit `fallthrough` is used; conditionless switch can express ranges. Range loops yield index and value copies. Ensure every loop progresses toward termination and test immediately below, at, and above each threshold.

lessons.title: Arrays, Slices, Maps, and Iteration
lessons.summary: Use arrays, slices, append, capacity, copying, maps, comma-ok lookup, range, and ownership-aware mutation.
objectives: Explain and apply Arrays, Slices, Maps, and Iteration
Test the contract with build and runtime evidence

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Arrays have fixed length and are values. A slice is a descriptor over an underlying array with length and capacity. `append` may reuse the current array or allocate a new one, so retain its returned slice. Sub-slices can keep a large backing array alive and can share mutable elements. Use `copy` when an independent snapshot is required. Maps provide key-value lookup; reading an absent key returns the value type's zero value, so use the comma-ok form when absence differs from a stored zero. Never write to a nil map.

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Functions can return multiple values, commonly a result and error. Go passes arguments by value; a pointer allows deliberate mutation of the pointed object but does not convey ownership. Structs group fields, and methods attach behavior to a named type. Keep fields unexported when updates must preserve invariants, and provide a constructor that validates initial state. Interfaces are satisfied implicitly by method sets. Define small interfaces at the consumer boundary and accept concrete types until substitution is actually useful. A nil interface and an interface containing a typed nil pointer are different.

lessons.title: Goroutines, Channels, Context, and a Tracker
lessons.summary: Combine goroutines, channels, synchronization, context cancellation, JSON, files, and tests in a race-safe persistent tracker.
objectives: Explain and apply Goroutines, Channels, Context, and a Tracker
Test the contract with build and runtime evidence

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: A goroutine runs concurrently and must have a defined completion and cancellation path. Channels communicate typed values and can coordinate ownership, but they are not required for every shared value. Only a sender should close a channel, and closing signals that no more values will arrive. Protect shared mutable state with confinement or synchronization and run tests with `go test -race`. `context.Context` carries cancellation and deadlines across call boundaries; pass it explicitly and do not store it in a struct. Validate decoded JSON before replacing trusted state and write files through a controlled boundary.

finalAssessment.instructionsMarkdown: Build a Go progress tracker using validated unexported models, slices and maps, explicit wrapped errors, JSON persistence, context-aware operations, controlled goroutine lifecycles, race-safe state, and at least ten table-driven tests.
